chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah, from a number of his companions, from Ali ibn Asbaat, from Yahya ibn Bashir al-Nabbal, who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said to my father: 'O Bashir! By what are you curing your sick ones?' He said, 'By these bitter medicines.' He said to him, 'No. When one of you is sick, take the white sugar, pound it, and pour cold water over it, and give it to him to drink, for the One Who made the healing in bitterness is Able to make it in sweetness.'
ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Sadiq recommend as a cure for illness instead of bitter medicines?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) challenges the prevailing Greco-Arabic medical theory of humors, which favored bitter remedies, by advocating for white sugar as a therapeutic agent. He grounds this practical advice in a theological principle: since God is the ultimate source of healing (*al-Shifa*), He is not bound by the sensory qualities of the remedy, demonstrating that sweetness can be as efficacious as bitterness. This reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on the flexibility of medical practice under divine permission rather than rigid adherence to specific material properties.
